newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas rises on storage trade, eases late.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas rises on storage trade, eases late.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices continued to strengthen early Wednesday on storage buying but then pared gains in late morning trade in response to forecasts for milder weather, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast prices gained more than five cents to the low-to-mid $2.60s early and then in the mid-$2.50s late, up an average of 20 cents from week-ago levels.

At the Henry Hub, La., most deals were confirmed done in the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s. In south Texas prices climbed into the $2.50-2.55 range as cool temperatures in the region prompted more buying interest.

Prices rose by about five cents in the Midcontinent where deals were reported done mostly in the mid-$2.40s. Forecasters are expecting temperatures to begin moderating Thursday in the region to levels slightly above-normal by the weekend.
The Chicago city-gate market showed signs of retreating as traders reported closing deals in the mid-to-high-$2.80s, as compared to the $2.88-2.91 range seen on Tuesday.
The strong western demand pushed Permian basin prices higher again into the low-to-mid $2.40s. Sources also attributed the rise to the early heating demand in Texas.
Similarly at the southern California border, prices climbed into the $2.50s, up at least five cents from Tuesday as the Canadian markets continued to demand substantial volumes of gas.

Oasis Pipe Line Co said it will curtail about 200 million cubic feet per day of gas in the first three weeks of November due to scheduled maintenance at the Prairie Lea Compressor Station in Caldwell County, Texas.
The outage is expected to end by November 21.
On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices remained strong in the high-$2.90s despite the mild weather in the Northeast.
